tldr: This is a loose thread of three unrelated pieces on running your own LLM inference server, not one developing event. It began with a hobbyist Qwen trainer-plus-server on Show HN (Nov 12) and an arXiv paper on Superfluid, a local server that distributes inference across devices (Nov 13).
whats_new: An APNIC post works through a 4-server, 8-GPU vLLM deployment of Llama 3.3 70B and argues request handling and session count, not GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, decide network design at that scale.
why_it_matters: For small self-hosted inference fleets, the bottleneck claim shifts sizing effort from interconnect spend toward request routing and concurrency limits.

beats.headline: Self-hosted servers: a Qwen hobby project and the Superfluid paper
beats.summary: Two early items frame local serving: one open-source trainer with a bundled server, one research system for spreading a model across local devices.

beats.headline: Few-node GPU inference: network design follows sessions, not bandwidth
beats.summary: A worked vLLM example on 8 GPUs across 4 servers moves the thread from single-box serving to small-cluster sizing.

open_questions: Does any vLLM or SGLang benchmark confirm that session count outweighs interconnect bandwidth for 70B-class models on 2–4 nodes?
Does Superfluid release code or measured latency against a single-GPU baseline?
take_for_builders: Before buying faster interconnect for a 2–4 node inference cluster, load-test your real concurrent session count and request mix against the current network first.
